clue.text: Moor the boat in this way outside Scottish town

indicators.note: outside tells us the phrase for 'in this way' wraps around the mooring verb

parts.note: by this means, or 'by', as in 'by doing so'
to moor a boat is to anchor it

explanation.surface: Instructions to tie up a boat just beyond a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: BANCHORY is a small town on the River Dee in Aberdeenshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Banchory is a real place in Aberdeenshire, so it is an example of a town in Scotland.

clue.text: This feline's made duck act uneasily

parts.note: to duck is to bob down quickly

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters of act are unsettled and shifted about

explanation.surface: A wild cat was produced from a nervous duck's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobcat is a North American lynx, a wild member of the cat family.

clue.text: Poverty the French provoke

parts.note: poverty is a state of need
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Poor French people stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to goad or irritate them on purpose.

clue.text: Sharpen your first search through labyrinth

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word your

parts.note: to comb an area is to search through it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Advice to whet your wits before hunting your way through a maze.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeycomb, by extension, is any intricate maze-like network of cells or passages.

clue.text: Howling wind that delights the shopkeeper?

explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind blowing hard could be called roaring; and booming business, the idiom for brisk sales, pleases any retailer.

clue.text: Unfortunate that first Cuban export is rebuffed

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word that
rebuffed means pushed back, so the Cuban export is read backwards

parts.note: Havana cigars are Cuba's famous export

explanation.surface: Sad news that Cuba's leading export has been turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' also tells us T comes at the front; 'is rebuffed' turns CIGAR into RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events are deeply unlucky or calamitous ones.

clue.text: Right to support two army units, though it's even less common

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits underneath the others

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery and RE the Royal Engineers, two British army corps
RA is the Royal Artillery and RE the Royal Engineers, two British army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier's remark that backing two regiments is even rarer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' places R below RA and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer is scarcer still, happening less often than another uncommon thing.

clue.text: Booking for jazz musician's caper? Stupendous!

parts.note: a gig is a booked engagement for a musician
an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.surface: A jazz player's lively stunt at a gig gets a gasp of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, and stupendous likewise means astonishingly great in size or degree.

clue.text: Come together to Congreve play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to attend a play by the Restoration dramatist William Congreve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun naming a Congreve drama, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge meet at a single point.

clue.text: I ban line-dancing for a two-year spell

indicators.note: dancing has the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forbids line dancing for two years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-dancing' reads as one hobby, but 'line' is part of the anagram and 'dancing' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Biennial describes something lasting, or recurring every, two years.

clue.text: For a start, has nothing to dress in

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, meaning nothing
to rig someone out is to dress them

explanation.surface: To begin with, a person owns no clothes to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something begins, its source or beginning.

clue.text: Hospitals not in situ — it's disturbing

indicators.note: disturbing means moving things out of place, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Moving patients out of their places is unsettling for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals are a kind of public establishment, often called institutions.

clue.text: Devalue colleague about nothing

indicators.note: about means going around, so the colleague word surrounds the nought

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or partner
O is the figure zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Belittling a coworker over a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: To alloy a precious metal is to mix in a baser one, debasing it, hence to lower its worth.

clue.text: Blissful state to be in?

parts.note: plays on the proverb that not knowing is bliss: the condition of being unaware is the happy one

explanation.surface: A question about where true happiness lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'where it is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise' makes not knowing a state of bliss.

clue.text: Pine substitute, note — it's stood the test of time

definitions.text: it's stood the test of time

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a stand-in is a substitute
G is one of the notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: An old pine tree, replaced and noted, still stands after many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something longstanding has lasted a long time, being well established.

clue.text: Fear of the aged? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Fear of the aged? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: Fear of the aged? Quite the opposite!
parts.note: the opposite of dreading what is old is dreading what is new or novel

explanation.surface: A quip about being afraid of elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is a dread of novelty, the reverse of fearing old things.

clue.text: Informed English journalist holds outdated currency

indicators.note: holds means the English journalist pair contains the coin

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist
the ducat was a gold coin used in Europe in past centuries

explanation.surface: A well-read English reporter carries old money.
explanation.walkthrough: The ducat, an old European gold coin, sits after the first E. 'Informed' is an adjective here, meaning knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means well informed through learning or schooling.

clue.text: Recoils from birds around the lake

indicators.note: around has the birds placed about the letter for lake

parts.note: finches are small songbirds
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks back from birds gathered round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to wince or shrink back, which is what one does in recoiling.

clue.text: Be it denial, or, put another way, circumspection?

indicators.note: put another way invites rearranging the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about whether denial is really caution in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put another way' looks like 'in other words', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful thought before acting, much like circumspection or caution.

clue.text: Girl friend turned up from Greece, we hear

parts.note: Greece sounds like grease, and fat is grease

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means the word for friend is read bottom to top

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A girl's friend arrives from Greece, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that Greece is heard as grease, which means FAT; 'turned up' gives IMA from AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima is a girl's given name, notably that of the Prophet Muhammad's daughter.

clue.text: Agree monsieur's cooked little

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman agrees that he has cooked only a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes EAGRE; 'little' is an adjective meaning scanty, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or small in amount.

clue.text: Agreement that firm has new surfacing put over road

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: put over means the surfacing layer is laid across the road and encloses it

parts.note: a coat of tarmac or paint is a surfacing layer

explanation.surface: A contracting firm wins a deal to resurface a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement or treaty, especially one between a state and the Church.

clue.text: Word that's rarely contradicted

parts.note: a term whose opposite is 'rarely', the word that denies it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a statement almost nobody argues with.
explanation.definitionFit: Its antonym is seldom, so contradicting 'rarely' gives frequently.

clue.text: With effort, lift to the skies, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word for the skies stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: the heavens are the skies above

explanation.surface: Raising something up towards the heavens with a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter N from HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul or raise something heavy with great exertion.

clue.text: Time on a smack, then I come to this island

parts.note: a smack is a hit or blow

explanation.surface: A sailor on a fishing smack reaches an island in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: TAHITI is the largest island of French Polynesia. A smack is also a fishing boat, which feeds the sea voyage picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a Pacific island, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: But, vacillating in action, having mixed feelings

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the word for action

parts.note: doing is activity or action

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters of but move about

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating while acting, torn between choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacillating' makes UBT. 'But' looks like a conjunction starting the sentence, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting means being uncertain, torn between belief and disbelief.

clue.text: Ill-treating?

parts.note: read not as abusing but as treating the ill, giving medicine to sick people

explanation.definitionFit: Giving patients measured amounts of medicine is how sick people are treated.

clue.text: Rocket case needs repair — behind schedule

indicators.note: needs repair suggests the word case is broken and must be put back together differently

parts.note: late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A rocket's casing must be fixed, and the launch is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs repair' turns CASE into ESCA. 'Rocket' is a verb meaning to soar.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that rocket rise sharply, which is to escalate rapidly.
